selectedDrugs.rule: An NDC-11 is on a year's list when the rows for it cover every day of the year, from the maximum fair price effective date to the end date (open when blank). A row that ends before it starts never applies. An NDC covered for only part of the year is listed under partial. The engine matches entries on the NDC-11 only. The drug name is there for people reading the file.

maximumFairPrices.rule: Each period is one data row of the CMS file in effect on some day of the year: its NDC-11, its maximum fair price effective date (from), its end date (to, null when blank) and its price per unit of the NDC-9. A row that ends before it starts records a deselection and is left out. The engine uses a period only when the fill date falls inside it, multiplies the unit price by the caller's quantity in NDC units and rounds the product to the cent.

manufacturerDiscount.note: CMS lists the labeler codes covered by a discount program agreement (C20, monthly back to January 2025 in C22) and the NDC-9s eligible for the phase-in (C21). A labeler code says which company made the agreement. It does not say whether FDA approved a product under an NDA or BLA, so it cannot tell whether a drug is an applicable drug. Phase-in drugs get a lower discount than the 2026 rates the engine holds. Neither list settles a drug's program, so it stays open.

citations.member: Manufacturer Discount Program Labeler Code ReadMe.pdf
citations.quote: Under the Manufacturer Discount Program, Medicare Part D only covers brand-name drugs and biologics with a labeler code that is covered by a Manufacturer Discount Program agreement.

citations.section: Section 40, labeler codes and non-applicable drugs
citations.quote: Part D coverage may be available for non-applicable drugs that otherwise meet the definition of a covered Part D drug, regardless of whether the labeler code of such drug is covered by a Discount Program agreement.

citations.member: Manufacturer Discount Program NDC-9 List ReadMe.pdf
citations.quote: Inclusion of an NDC-9 on the list means that the drug is eligible for phase-in when covered under Part D; it does not constitute a coverage determination or supersede any relevant Medicare or plan coverage criteria.

insulin.note: None of the CMS pages checked publishes a list of covered insulin products by NDC or RxCUI. The selected-drug list holds one insulin family (C16) because it was selected, not because it is insulin, so it is not used to classify insulin.
